Using \(\sin A=\cos B=\sin(\frac\pi2-B)\), we have
\[
\sin(\pi\cos x)=\sin\left(\frac\pi2-\pi\sin x\right).
\]
Thus
\[
\pi\cos x=\frac\pi2-\pi\sin x+2\pi k
\]
or
\[
\pi\cos x=\pi-\left(\frac\pi2-\pi\sin x\right)+2\pi k
=\frac\pi2+\pi\sin x+2\pi k.
\]
Dividing by \(\pi\):
\[
\cos x+\sin x=\frac12+2k
\]
or
\[
\cos x-\sin x=\frac12+2k.
\]
Since \(\sin x\pm\cos x\in[-\sqrt2,\sqrt2]\), the only possible integer \(k\) is \(k=0\). So
\[
\sin x+\cos x=\frac12
\]
or
\[
\cos x-\sin x=\frac12.
\]

For \(\sin x+\cos x=\frac12\),
\[
(\sin x+\cos x)^2=\frac14
\]
\[
1+\sin 2x=\frac14
\]
\[
\sin 2x=-\frac34.
\]

For \(\cos x-\sin x=\frac12\),
\[
(\cos x-\sin x)^2=\frac14
\]
\[
1-\sin 2x=\frac14
\]
\[
\sin 2x=\frac34.
\]

Therefore all possible values are
\[
-\frac34,\frac34.
\]

The answer is \(-\frac34,\frac34\).
